utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please be seated. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good morning to you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, also in my team, Mr. Gramsci di Fazio, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you and your team. I apologise to you for starting later than envisaged. The reason is I was busy on another case earlier on and we had a few things to discuss. Of course, we did not have the chance to discuss them before. We have discussed them now, but it took us a little bit longer than we had anticipated. So any preliminaries? I see none. None? Yes, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just this, I suppose. We considered the position yesterday about tendering documents which are not exhibits but which -- the originals of which are in the possession of the Prosecution, and taking into account, of course, the fact that the Trial Chamber may want to look at those documents during their deliberations and the fact that the Prosecution doesn't seem to have any opposition to us tendering documents into their possession. On the contrary, they wish us to. We don't oppose that course of action, tendering those documents. Of course with the reserve that we are not tendering them with the truth of their contents or to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That will be addressed also in our filing of authenticity. So that concerns two documents I don't know if we should do it now or at the end --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the number, or the ERN number. Please, we will need your help.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I have those. I have those numbers. The first was 02075704 to 02075705, and that was S-2. I stand to be corrected if that's wrong but that's the note I have. And the second one was S-3, and the ERN was 02075701. And then there will be a couple of more today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What's your position on this, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we accept, of course, but very important is that the copy will be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We are speaking a different language, my dear. The copy is of no use to anyone. Copy is of no use to anyone. We don't need copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, can it be a combination both the copy and the original?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Provided we have the original. I mean, I don't -- I don't really care how many copies are made of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, S-2 and S-4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to help me there because I must confess that taking the position that each one of you took yesterday, I didn't bother to jot down the reference of the ERN number or the S- number, so you need to help us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let me first take a look, Your Honour, to the ERN. Perhaps my learned friend can help me out. This is related to file 808. These are the source documents Mr. Jones related to Naser Oric signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's -- can we -- who has them? You still have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We are referring to documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Madam Registrar has them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are the two. So Usher, I wish -- I would like you to go around and make sure that the parties agree that these are the documents. Once that is done, hand them to us and we will provide accordingly. But first I want to make sure that we are talking of the right documents because I don't want to make a mistake there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, please also tell us what that would be by way of S- or S-full stop. I think it's S-.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's S-2; 02075704 to 02075705. That's S-2. That's his handwritten document related to Kostadin Popovic, and we certainly agree that that can be tendered. And then the second one is S-3; it's 02075701. And that's a typed document relating to Kostadin Popovic, and that's the other -- yes, that's the other document. I can confirm neither are exhibits yet, and we are happy for them to be Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So let's deal with these two documents. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I agree, except the S-2 and S-3 related to Hamed Salihovic as such can be handed over and tendered, and in the later stage a copy of it can be substituted whenever it needed for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but we'll take care of that ourselves in our decision. Can I have the two documents, please. And let me make the entry now. So the first document to be entered in exhibit, as a Defence Exhibit is an original document bearing ERN 02075704 and on its retro, 02075705. This is a document consisting in one paper, sheet of paper, with handwriting on both sides. This document is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D1014 with the understanding that the Prosecution has agreed to its tendering only on an animo ritirandi basis. In other words, a copy will be made of it and entered into the records together with this original and marked as D1014.1, and when either this Trial Chamber, or any other Chamber for that matter, no longer requires this document, the original in other words, the original, such original will be returned by the Registrar to the Prosecutor of this Tribunal upon a simple demand, upon a simple demand, to be communicated both to Chamber and to the lead counsel of the accused or the accused himself. The second document to be tendered consists of one page, with ERN - correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Wubben or Mr. Jones - 02075 -- what's this, 5701, 5701, and it's being marked as Defence Exhibit D1015 and as such is being tendered and received on the same basis and conditions as the previous document. So until we need this it will stay with us. The moment we don't need it any longer, we or any other Tribunal, then you have a right to claim it back and you only need to put a simple demand, request for it. All right? For the record also, the first of these documents, that is D1014, is referred to in expert Bilic's testimony as S-2 or -2 while Defence Exhibit D1015 is referred to as Defence -- in Professor Bilic's report as S-3. So here you are. Yes. I saw Mr. Jones looking at the clock. I don't blame you. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, in fact, I was just wondering when the breaks would be. I presume --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The breaks will be at 11.30. There will only be one break obviously. We can have it at 11.30 or quarter to 11.00 -- sorry, not 11.00 -- yeah, quarter to 12.00, either 11.30 or quarter to 12.00. Whenever it's convenient. And, of course, the recorder will tell us if he's getting tired because this is a particularly tiring testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are finally ready to proceed with your testimony. Please make yourself comfortable. There is no need to make the solemn declaration again. The one you made yesterday remains valid before the entirety or throughout the entirety of your testimony. Mr. Jones will proceed with his examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And good morning from me, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, yesterday, when we left off we were just coming to S-7. So if the witness could please be shown that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And for the record, the ERN is 02075714, and it's actually P51.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's starts at page 7 of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if the witness could also have a copy of his report in front of him, please, which is now D1012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, is this in evidence or not? It isn't, I take it, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This next document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it is actually P51, you're saying, yeah, okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I didn't want to raise the issue, Your Honour, because it may raise any more problems. But Your Honour will notice that some of the documents which are already exhibits will be copies in your file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So another solution will have to be found for you to have access to knows originals, but that's a matter for you obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this document, as with all the Hamed Salihovic documents, was available in the original; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And we can see that it's handwritten. And is it in the same format as any of the other documents that you looked at?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The other handwritten documents.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, what can you say about who wrote this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handwritten content of this document was written by the writer we have labelled as X1.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was one writing implement used on this document or more than one?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written in ink.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the first part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the first part of the answer. The question put to you, Professor Bilic, was: Thank you. Now, was one writing implement used on this document or more than one? What was your answer? Could you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] More than one was used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the signature and the stamp. Is the stamp in the usual or in the normal place?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Comparing this with the other contentious documents investigated, the stamp is in an unusual position. It's in the central part of the document quite far to the left from the signature so that it looks a bit odd.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And your conclusions as to the handwriting and signature on this document are on page 36, paragraphs 1 and 2 of your report, and if you could just confirm those, that the handwriting is most probably not that of Hamed Salihovic and the signature is most probably not that of Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I abide by this, this conclusion, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to clarify me, Professor Bilic, do I understood you correctly that everything what is handwritten on this document is written from the same hand, so to say, or are there two different handwritings and, if so, which ones are different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this contentious document, there is the handwriting of only one writer. But it was not written continuously. The handwritten part I will indicate now is written at a later date and using a different pen, while this part up here, this part, was written using another pen, and later on there is another handwritten text written in a different pen. However, the handwriting is the product of a single writer in the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But does this mean that the last line before the signature, although it is written with a different ink, that the writing, handwriting, is the same as it is in the upper part? So the only difference is in the ink but the handwriting, according to your expertise, is from the same person? Just to make --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, the next document is S-8 or S-8. It's 02075760. It's P66, and it's dealt with at page 12 of your report, Professor Bilic. Again, it's a handwritten document. There is no stamp on this occasion. First of all, what can you tell us about the paper on which this document is written and the other documents which are only handwritten?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document also requires a brief explanation. The paper size is the standard A4. It's paper used both for handwriting and typing. On this document, several different writing implements are used. This part up to here is written continuously at a stretch. This part was added subsequently using a different pen. And finally, at the bottom, there is an addition, the words, "Died, 9th of March 1993." On the right-hand side, there is one of the versions of a signature. This document does not bear a round stamp. Alterations have been made, as is evident, in the date and here as well, something has been crossed out in ball-point pen, and then the words "directly responsible" have been added at a later date, so this is a document that was not written continuously. The writer of this part -- do you see what I'm pointing at? I think you all do. This part was written by the writer we have labelled X1, whereas the brief note in the bottom left-hand part is the handwriting of the writer we have labelled X2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And for the record, because reading the transcript later we won't be able to see this clearly, are you saying that X2 wrote the part which says, "Died 9.3.93," and the rest of the document is written by X1?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if the witness could please be shown S-9A which we looked at yesterday while keeping that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I would ask you on this document which is now being placed to your right, Professor Bilic, to go down to just number 1, in fact, where we see the same name Jakov Djokic, and the words written to the left, "umro, 09.03," is that the same words and the same writer, or are they different?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is writer X2, as we have labelled him, next to number 1, where it says Djokic, Jakov.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And I think we perhaps haven't quite confirmed your conclusions yet for S-8. So going back to that document, your conclusions are on page 36, paragraphs 1 and 2, that the handwriting is most probably not Hamed Salihovic, the signature most probably not Hamed Salihovic, and then you also say the signature is by X1, I believe. If you could confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the handwriting of X1, as we said, and the note at the bottom was added on by X2, if that's what you were referring to. Most probably it was not Hamed Salihovic who wrote this, nor did he most probably sign these notes and this handwriting on these two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I might have misspoken about the signature of X1. Is it correct in fact you didn't draw conclusions as to whether the signature was by X1 or X2 because you didn't analyse the signature, the other signatures of X1 or X2?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: X1 and X2 are unknown persons. That's why we labelled them as such, so I had nothing to compare the signature with, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can usher please bring us this S-8, not S-9, S-8, the witness had seen before, and the previous witness -- the previous document, the original, P51, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's just for your information that sometimes it is conveyed what you're speaking about through the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. All right. Let's [Microphone not activated] the witness any further or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Not with this document. We are on to S-9 now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's S-9, 02075763. And that's P108, and it's dealt with on page 13 of Professor Bilic's report. This document has no stamp and no signature and so it's simply a question of who wrote on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you could tell us, please, Professor.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handwritten content of this document, this one that I'm indicating now, was written by writer X1. He keeps recurring in these documents as does X2, who added on the note, "Died on the 10th of March." That was written by X2. This was written on standard A4 paper of no special quality. This text here was added on later with a different or, rather, with a third pen, so here we have three different ball-point pens that were used. This was added on and the entire document was not written continuously at a stretch. So there is no continuity in the handwriting of either one or the other writer. I hope I've been clear. I can clarify further, if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no stamp, no signature, which is inconsistent with the set of documents under investigation. However, that's for the Court to evaluate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. One matter, you read the part written by X2 as died 10 March. Is that -- is that in fact what's written there or what? The English translation I note we have October 1993. Can you read that for us, Professor, whether it's -- is it 10th of March and then something, or is it October 1993?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this document, if that's the document you are referring to, it says, in the Latin script, "Died, 10.03.9." That's what it says. 10.03.9 ... so the year is not complete. This can be clearly seen here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Just to have it clarified for sure, so there is no way that that could be in your understanding 10.93, godina [phoen]? You exclude the possibility of having instead of what you said, 10.93, godina, "g" as sometimes is used in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me clarify again. The word "died" is handwritten here followed by the number 10, which means the 10th day in the month. The month is 03; that's March. This is 03. You can see that the 0s are the same. They are written in the same way. Then there follows a full stop after 3 and then the number 9, and we do not know what year this is because the year is incomplete. It's quite clear that it says, "Died, 10.03.9." I think I've clarified now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: As far as the handwriting on this document is concerned your conclusion is on page 36, paragraph 1, most probably not Hamed Salihovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I finished with that document, and we can move on to S-9A, and that's 01239581 to 01239583. And that's P19.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's dealt with on pages 13 to 14 of your report, Professor Bilic.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not investigate this document. I'm not familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If you look at the first page, now, can you tell us first of all is there a water-mark on this page?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which document are you referring to? A moment ago there was another one on the ELMO. Are you referring to that one or this one? Please be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. It's a three-page document, and that's the first page of it and then the other two pages are with it. And I'm just asking you about the first page, which is 01239581. It will be passed to you in a moment. That page which you've looked at several times already. I'm just something you about that page.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the document? Please take a look at the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And is there a water-mark on that page, firstly?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I stated in my report on page 13, there is a water-mark here. You can see it through transmitted light. It is a silhouette of a sail-boat, like the one we saw in some documents yesterday. You can see it very nicely. Down the middle, there are continuous water-marks of sail-boats.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, we can see that this document is obviously typewritten with handwriting on the left margin and elsewhere. You've told us about some of that handwriting already. What did you conclude about X1 and X2 or other writers on this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What specifically are you asking me? I concluded that both writers participated here, X1 and X2. They are constant participants recurring in these documents. Next to 30 we have handwriting by X1. Here it is. This was added on later. Then we have a signature. In the left-hand margin, there are alternating notes in the handwriting of X1 and X2, and I can tell you point by point which handwriting it is. So we have X1 and X2 alternating here. There are two writers participating here persistently, X1 and X2. Next to number 30, the addition here was written by X1. At 29, the typewritten name was put in subsequently, whereas next to number 28, the name is typed continuously with a number. There is a lot more that could be said about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We are going to come to those points one by one. If you go to number 17 where it says Rado Pejic, can you read what's written to the left and also tell us who wrote those remarks?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to number 17 is the typewritten last name Pejic, Mihajlo Rado. On the left-hand side, there is a brief note added by writer X2, who write, "Died between the 17th and 18.03.93."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, at the bottom of the document we see brown marks. What can you tell us about those markings? Or that disintegration, if you like?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is physical and chemical destruction of the document along the bottom and the lower right-hand corner. A piece of paper has been torn off. There is an interesting point here. As the destruction was physical and chemical, it is to be expected -- it would have been -- to be expected that the handwriting and the signature would also be damaged. However, after the physical, chemical destruction of the document, number 30 was added on, Djukic (Arsen) Milomir, imprisoned or captured in Kravica, followed by the date and the signature and a round seal, a round stamp, that is. This was added on in ball-point pen and there is no destruction. There is no bleeding of ink. If a chemical destroyed the paper but did not destroy the writing, this is evidence that the writing was added on subsequently, as was the stamp, and a new version of the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we have a look at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I've clarified sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. At least on my part, I'm happy with his explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, I'll explore --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: One matter is that you described --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Do you wish to see the document, Mr. Wubben, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please feel free. They are your documents, after all. Any time you wish to see them, please let us know. Sorry, Mr. Jones, for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Not at all, Your Honour. Perhaps I can proceed to the next question, though, while the Prosecution inspect the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You mentioned just now a new version of the signature and on S-8, I think it was, you referred to a version of the signature. What do you mean by that, that you've come across different versions of the alleged Hamed Salihovic signature in these documents?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is it usual or unusual for someone to use different types of signature around the same time, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It makes no sense. It's non-sensical.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. In fact -- well, perhaps just to explore that a little further. Are there circumstances where you encounter someone using different types, different versions of one signature, any specific circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came across that phenomenon in the case of criminals who wish to protect themselves, who use different versions of signature. However, in this particular case, these signatures were written freely, without paying particular attention to them being consistent with one another. They are spontaneous signatures of these writers and, of course, every person uses one version of signature throughout his or her life. They would rarely use several versions. If a person has to sign thousands of documents every day, then the person will tend to use initials rather than a full signature or in any case it will be a simplified version to enable the person to sign the documents as fast as possible. There may also exist an obligation in that respect. For instance, in a bank, you cannot use two types of signature. You have to deposit your signature for the purposes of bank transactions and then the signature has to be the same as that which was deposited. Any change in signature will be immediately noticed by the bank staff, for instance, if one wishes to make a transaction with their account. It may happen that a person signs in full both the first and the last name, but then this is no longer a signature. It's rather a piece of handwriting. We said yesterday that a handwriting comes before one's signature because one first learns to write and then forms his or her signature, but then, in time, through use, this becomes an automatic and consistent process. If people were to change their signatures whenever it crossed their minds, then signatures would be under constant suspicion and examination. A signature is an identifying mark. It's as important as a finger-print. That's why a person cannot change one's -- his or her signature day in, day out. Changes may only be brought about by some sort of a physical handicap or a drug addiction or any other such influence. Otherwise, one's signature never changes in life. That is why variations in signature over a short span of time, especially in documents such as these ones, showed that they are merely improvisations. That would be my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And how many versions of the Hamed Salihovic signature did you come across in these specimens you looked at?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When examining these pieces of handwriting, we will not say that they are Hamed Salihovic's signatures; we merely assume so. Every piece of writing there differs from others in this or that aspect. Only a visual examination shows that they are not identical, which does not make any sense. If you take a look at the set of documents here and if you take a look at the signatures there, you will see that they are mutually different to a great extent, especially the ones that are -- seem to be shortened pieces of writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry to cut you off, Professor, but we need to make progress, and it was really -- I was looking more for a figure. On page 14 of your report, for example, you referred to a fourth version of the alleged Hamed Salihovic signature so my question was really that. Are there four versions or five or three? How many versions of this alleged signature did you discover?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this was the fourth version, as I called it, because it differed greatly from the others. For the purposes of clarity and understanding of these signatures which are purported to be those of Hamed Salihovic, I termed it as the fourth version. I did not go into detail on the matter of versions because what mattered to me was whether Hamed Salihovic wrote them or not. However, a lot more could have been written about this. I only went as far as I thought was necessary for the purposes of examination. I could have then said that this was a fifth or a sixth version, but I believed that this much would suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we will just take the next few points as briefly as possible. On this document which we are still looking at, S-9A, there appears to be a stamp at the top where we can at least see "strogo povjerljivo"? Do you see that in the top right-hand corner? And if you can't say this, did you find that stamp on any other documents which you analysed?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not find this on any other document. This is a trace of a stamp, which is quite poorly visible in the top part. It says, "Military secret, strictly confidential." Based on my experience, this could be seen on military documents, both on the envelope and the document itself, but it usually also contained an additional part which could be filled in to write the reference number and so on and so forth, the date. Here, this was affixed only to show that this was a document that was a military secret, strictly confidential. However, it does not contain the number of the document or the date. This, however, is contained in the top left-hand corner. However, such stamps as this one usually contained an additional part which would state their reference number and their date. As the document is now, we could say that it is strictly confidential but in the other aspect it is not. It does have its official reference number, 108, and the date is the 3rd of February. We can say that this is the first time I see this type of rectangular stamp in purple ink. Anything else in connection with this, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally, just to confirm the -- your conclusion about the signature, most probably not Hamed Salihovic as set out on page 36, paragraph 2 of your report.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most probably not signed by Hamed Salihovic himself, based on what we see here as the signature but we don't know whose handwriting this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is only on one side. There is no handwriting on the reverse side. The entire side is typed out, but we have handwritten notes, a signature and stamp. This document also carries a water-mark, as is written in my report, across the central part there is the continuous silhouette of a sail-boat, and you can take a look if you so wish. Later on this will prove quite significant. I don't know if Their Honours are interested in taking a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Their Honours will let you know if they wish to see it. utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see for yourselves that this part was additionally typed. This can be seen quite easily. You see the text on the left-hand side should aligned with the text on the right-hand side but it is not, and this is a clear indication of the text having been written subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is it right or not that the spacing also is different on the -- what's written to the left and what's written on the right, spacing between the lines?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is quite evident, can easily be seen at first sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think we can move fairly quickly to your conclusions. First of all, at the bottom we have the words "razmjenjen 7.01.93," "exchanged 7.01.93," is that X1, X2 or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the handwriting of X2, which says, "Exchanged on the 7th of February 1993." Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And yesterday you were telling us about the grammar in which these documents are written. utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not one of the tasks that I had to address. However, it is replete with grammatical errors, the semantics, the spelling, and when you take a look at it does seem quite illegible at least -- or unintelligible at least as far as the language itself is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When you read the entire contents --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the witness. He said that it seems very, very illiterate, and this was not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What did you exactly provide as an answer to the question that was put to you, Professor Bilic? What were your comments on the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

This part which says, these parts, the last sentence, the entire context, the word order seems quite confusing, although this is not part of my expertise but there are many grammatical errors, there are many alterations and corrections that could be noticed by a person analysing this in great detail. This is my generic assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think it's clear enough. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then proceeding to your conclusions, as set out on page 36, paragraph 2, the signature most probably not that of Hamed Salihovic and the handwritten notes not by Hamed Salihovic. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not write the text or sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tried to follow page 36, what my learned friend asked for a kind of confirmation and I'm glad -- I'm happy when Defence counsel lead, but the confirmation was not to the full extent confirmed. utterances.speaker: MR. JONES

utterances.text: I think the question was very simple. I mean, he was referred to page 36 of his report and a suggested conclusion in that page, that the signature was probably -- was not that or is not that of Hamed Salihovic.

utterances.text: Yes. It's paragraph 2, most probably, and that's S-10, not signed by Hamed Salihovic, and then also S-10 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you confirm it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do confirm that. Most probably not written by Hamed Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you explained yesterday but it might just be useful to put on the record again today that you used the most probably measure because the non-contentious samples which you had were 20 years before the contentious samples and for that reason you didn't feel you could give a firm [Realtime transcript read in error: "fair"] conclusion? utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's a fair summary. And I explained this in my findings and I explained it verbally here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the transcript, I said a firm conclusion rather than a fair conclusion. That was page 24, line 7. utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was typed out on A4 paper, which also carries a water-mark containing a silhouette of a sail-boat. This means that this type of paper was used in this set of documents. utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe that is all for now. There is nothing written on the reverse side.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And your conclusions, again, just to confirm them, the signature most probably not Hamed Salihovic and the handwriting --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably not signed by Hamed Salihovic himself, and most probably he did not make those handwritten notes in the form of dates or words.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And we've compared this document already with S-9A, so I won't do that again. I'll move on to S-12, which is 02075742. In fact, if the witness -- if that last document could be kept with the witness, or beside him. Yes, S-12, and that's dealt with at page 14 of Professor Bilic's report. Now, I asked that S-11 be kept with you because I think you say in your report that S-11 is a carbon-copy of S-12; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Dealing now with S-12, again can you confirm any water-mark?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, there is a continuous silhouette of a sail-boat as was the case with the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you said this is a carbon-copy but is it correct that in fact the handwritten corrections and the stamp and the signature are in different places on this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct. This can easily be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And apart from that, you -- did you reach the same conclusions with regard to this document as with the previous document in terms of the features which you described for S-11? And you don't need to rehearse them all. If it's the same, then that's fine. If there is something else to add, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document contains a different short note written by X2, which says, "Buried in the cemetery," whereas the earlier document said, "Died between the 17th and the 18th." I will try to place them next to each other. That's it. This is a carbon-copy, and this is the first version. This document contains the text which says, "Died between the 17th and the 18th March 1993." The other document says, "Buried in the cemetery." It's -- the same person is involved, Pejevic, Rado -- Pejic, Rado, and you can take a look at the dates. And this is an absurdity because it's the same text, which has to do with the same person, but the texts differ. One would expect the texts to be the same as well, since the two documents are otherwise identical. The location of both the signature and the stamp is different. Here again, almost the entire half of the signature is covered by the stamp. We have the instances of additional writing at the top, so we would say that they have -- share the same genesis, the two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And your conclusions are as with the previous document and as set out on page 36 --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I said most probably not signed by Hamed Salihovic. That's in point 2. Point 1, most probably not written by Hamed Salihovic. And this refers to the short handwritten notes which were not written by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I ask you one final question on this document and on S-11? We see in the last sentence, the word "uhvacen." I appreciate this isn't something which you necessarily addressed as an expert but is that a word used by Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser would like to know the meaning of that word.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Captured. The word means, in the Bosnian, arrested, but the variant "uhicen," the variant of the word arrested, is Croat, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What word is used by Bosnians, sorry, just again for the record, for "captured"?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The version in Bosnian would be "uhvachen" or -- which means arrested, or "zarobljen," taken prisoner. These are synonyms, but these are the words that would be used in the Bosnian version. "Uhvacen" or "zarobljen," although I would prefer -- I think "zarobljen" would be in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To make the record clear, could the word in Bosnian, the word used by the expert, be recorded because otherwise we have an interpretation, because the expert said that the word "uhicen" is not the one used in the Bosnian, but rather "uhvacen" -- "uhvacen."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, "uhvacen," "zarobljen."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We can perhaps also correct that during the break with the court reporter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you can do that during the break, because otherwise it will take us five minutes to dictate.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I'm finished with this document although we have the same issue as before that it's not currently an exhibit. utterances.text: It's up to you. I mean, you know what the position is. We cannot force the Defence to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We will tender it if it hasn't been tendered already, and I'm sure the Registry can check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In my opinion, it's not tendered so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. If it's not tendered, you wish to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that would become D1016; correct? And it's being tendered and received on the same conditions as in the case of the previous two documents, D1014 and 1015.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And subject to our same reserves about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we can now move on to S-12A, and that is 02075743. And it's dealt with on -- it's also P62, and it's dealt with on page 13 of Professor Bilic's report. All right. Actually, I'm informed it may be helpful for the record that the document we just saw is in fact part of D155 but not in English, just the B/C/S version. So that might be of assistance at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So now looking at this document, we can probably deal with this quite shortly, although in fact I would ask Professor, if you could open page 23 of your report because I believe you -- that shows a map which you described for this -- which you carried out on this document.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We'll just have a look at that and you can briefly explain.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document marked S-12A; is that right? Yes. This one. The contentious handwriting was photographed on this document, and fortunately a word was found, "zemljoradnik," meaning farmer or farm labourer, and in this form, N.5, which is an uncontentious text, handwritten text, we find this same word as his father's occupation, and this is indubitably written by Hamed Salihovic, so we can compare the same word. We have shown only the most prominent features in these two handwritten versions of this word. And you can see that there is absolutely a difference here. I have marked some other differences as well here, and this is another one of the elements that goes to confirm that the handwritten content of this, that is this document, was not written by Hamed Salihovic. It's not his handwriting. I have documented this on this map here, and you can take a look. I wanted the Court and everyone in the courtroom to observe this and to see for themselves. This is the best way. When you look at the signature on this document, this is again one of the versions with a stamp and again we have the handwriting here, which is most probably not written in the hand of Hamed Salihovic. And under one, there is another signature probably not written in the hand of Hamed Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: X1 was the writer of this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said that -- I said that when we were discussing 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did you say this is another version of the signature?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the versions, that's what I said. There is more than one. This is one of the versions of the signature recurring in these documents. They give the impression of a signature. I see that this was meant to give the impression of the signature, but they are all different. Nothing is consistent. Nothing is constant. Every time there is something different. And you can see that even if you're not a graphologist and have no skills as a graphologist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. We finished with that document. I might just deal with one more before the break. And that would be S-13. And it's 01321045 to 01321046. And I'd ask you to tell us, Professor, whether this document first of all has a water-mark, and if so, what type of water-mark?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me check once again. This is a very rare water-mark. Extra Post, a chamois on a rock. It's very high quality writing paper, and this water-mark is found only on this document. utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Just want to ask you one question. Yesterday -- yes, we were looking at S-2 and you mentioned seeing a chamois on a rock water-mark in that document as well. Is that the same image or a different one?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's different. This heraldic water-mark of a chamois was present on high quality paper produced by the Radece factory in Slovenia, which also produced paper for bank documents. Producers change their water-marks. We can say that this was --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. But so then on S-2, we have a water-mark with a chamois on a rock but also on this document but it's a different version of that water-mark; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what I said. The content was different as well. It said "Extra Post," whereas this one says, "Extra Post" continuously. You can take a look at it if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally before the break, your conclusion, the handwriting, because it's only a question of handwriting, there is no signature, most probably not that of Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably it is not the handwriting of Hamed Salihovic. This is the handwriting of the writer we have labelled X3. utterances.text: Yes. I don't know if it's tendered or not, this document. Is it tendered, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
