utterances.text: The very word, "control of Muslim forces," "controlja muslimanski snaga," [phoen] shows that this cannot be a document belonging to the Muslim forces. They certainly wouldn't have phrased it in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that observation. Now, as far as this document is concerned, it's again typed with some handwritten additions. Have you identified who made the handwritten additions?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have identified the writer whom we previously labelled as X2. For example, next to number 22, 22, it says, "Killed, Dimitrovski, Krste and wife," and then in the handwriting of X2 it says, "Killed." Next to number 16 where it says, "Lazic, Dusan Krsto," it's not the same one the Serbs say. We cannot attribute this to X2. This is a different person who wrote this. Also next to number 3, "Zivanovic, Jove Bogdan," it says here, "Died," this was written by X2, who occurs frequently, but above this we also have the word "razmjenjen," which means exchanged, and this was written by a different person. So here we have participation by X2 and another writer who does not occur frequently in these documents. On page 2 of the same document, next to number 38, we have the word double, "dupli." This was written by X2. Next to 40 it says, "u dupli," in double. And then 43, "Djokic, Vidosava, Jakov," says "double." Then we have number 39. Next to it says, "Exchanged at Lake Ziga." [phoen] This is a handwriting we cannot attribute to either X1 or X2 or X3. This is something completely different. That's what I can say about this document. It was typed on a single sheet of paper on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And it might be necessary just to clarify one matter. Next to 39, as I heard you in Bosnian, you read, "razmjenjen na Jezerv Ziv." Is that correct? "Exchanged at Jezero, lives," rather than the name of the lake as it came out in the English translation, interpretation.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says that he's alive. That's next to number 39, Mr. Jones. Yes. Next to 39. Not 32. On page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikolic, Pajo, Ratko, Pajo Ratko, it says, "Exchanged at Jezero," and then it says "alive," referring to Nikolic, Pajo, Ratko, that he's alive. I think I've been clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's clear. And then just finally did you analyse this handwriting by reference to non-contentious handwriting of Hamed Salihovic, and did you conclude it was most probably not written by Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Professor Bilic, you're being asked to speak into the microphone as well, please.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I said under 1 that Hamed Salihovic most probably did not write this in his own hand, this contentious handwritten document with short notes and additions. That's what it says precisely under 3, Hamed Salihovic most probably did not write this in his own hand. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I'm finished with that document and we will now move to the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this in evidence already, this document, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. So again it would be a question, sorry, of asking for an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I have the exhibit, the document, please, Usher? I thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, which consists of two sheets of paper, the first one of which has a crossed ERN 01837363, and underneath in handwriting, another reference number, ERN, which is 01837364, the second page having an ERN number 01837364-A, in capital form, is being tendered by the Defence, marked as Defence Exhibit D1018, under the same terms and conditions as all the previous documents tendered today from D1014.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The other thing is we would like to, because we are not experts, so if the witness can tell us if there are any water-marks here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't see any but, you know, sometimes they are hidden to the amateur eye.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I'll have one matter to clarify as well with the Professor on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, looking at those two piece of paper, do you see any water-mark by any chance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no water-marks on these two sheets of paper. This is plain writing paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There is a matter I'd like you to clarify for us. In your conclusions on page 36, at paragraph 4, you conclude that S-14 and also S-15, the document we'll see in the moment, were most probably written by two frequently participating writers marked as X1 and X2, and you've told us that X1 and X2 are not Hamed Salihovic. If I refer to paragraph 1, it appears that in fact you didn't specifically address S-14 and S-15 and say that they were not -- that they were most probably not written in hand by Hamed Salihovic. Does that follow anyway from the fact that X1 and X2 are not Hamed Salihovic? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. X1 and X2, when they are mentioned, that always means that most probably it is not the handwriting of Hamed Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document and we can now move on to S-15, which I believe is the last of the Hamed Salihovic documents, and that, for the record, is 01837373 to 01837375. And, again, it's not an exhibit and we will propose to tender it. Again, it's a list, and the title -- sorry, one moment. We can see the title for ourselves. Now this document is dealt with at page 15 of your report. And, again, if you could just tell us whom you identified as having done the handwriting in this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a list of fighters of the army of Republika Srpska who were captured or missing on the territory under the control of the Muslim forces from Srebrenica. Analysing the handwritten notes next to number 1, it says, "Not known" in handwriting, and then next to 3, it says, "Buried."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I can ask you to go through all the handwriting because there is quite a lot there. I would ask you to go to numbers 91 and 92, which is right at the end, and if you could first of all read what is handwritten there and then tell us who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Next to 91 -- just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you zoom in on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if you could read what that says and then --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It says here, "After, "poslije." "After demilitarisation," "demilitarizacije," and there is a bracket here, and it says, "posle demilitarizacije." "After demilitarisation." It is not in the Ijakavian dialect spoken in Bosnia, which would be "poslije," but rather "posle." This is significant. "Posle" is in the Ekavian dialect. It should be in the Ijakavian dialect. After that it says "demilitarizacije," demilitarisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is it the Ekavian dialect used or by whom is it used?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ekavian dialect is used in Serbia. They speak the Ekavian dialect. In Bosnia they seek Ijakavian.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you identify that writer or designated --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This writer has been identified. It's X2.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, actually, sorry, if we go back to 2, I'm not sure if you had told us yet, but for 2, if you look over past the second column, we see handwritten, 31.7.1993, 31 July 1993. And who in your opinion is the writer of that date?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably a third person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Now there is no signature, but again if you can just confirm your conclusions about the handwriting, which is -- again, it's page 36, paragraph 4, that the handwriting was most probably X1 and X2, neither of whom are Hamed Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's correct. That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, that concludes our examination of the documents allegedly written or signed by Hamed Salihovic. So we can now turn to those allegedly signed by Naser Oric. And we can start --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is not in --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies, yes, again that needs to be tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. So this document consists of three pages with the following ERN numbers: 0 -- first page 01837373; second page, 01827374; third page 01838385. The three pages are being tendered and received in evidence as Defence Exhibit D1018 -- 9, 1019. And they are being tendered and received under the same terms and conditions of the previous five documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. So we can turn now to S.1, and as explained, the point documents concern Naser Oric and Hamdija Fejzic. Now, this is 02075809, and it's P74. And this is also questioned signature Q2, and it's dealt with at pages 15 to 16 of Professor Bilic's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, firstly, Professor Bilic, is it right that this was available in the original, by which I mean it was not a photocopy or a carbon, that it was not a photocopy?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my investigation, I had access to the original of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, again is this written on only on one side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you tell us anything about the top right-hand column, "vojna tajna strogo pov," when that was written on the document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was added on subsequently, just as we have seen previously in other documents. When we looked at the other documents we saw this. It's not a continuous text, as you can see, but it was typed in later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now turning to the signatures at the bottom, what can you tell us about which writing implements were used for the alleged signatures of Fejzic and Oric?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The signature of Hamdija Fejzic is written in ball-point pen, leaving a dark blue ink trace, whereas Naser Oric's signature is written in ink. This is fountain-pen ink. It's a completely different kind of writing implement and it's covered over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll come that in a moment. In terms of those different writing implements, are there different pressures which are used when those implements are used and, if so, is that something you can analyse if you have the originals?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is an indispensable part of the investigation. I have to explain briefly that for a ball-point pen, to function properly, there has to be a certain amount of pressure. A ball-point pen will not write unless pressure is exerted, whereas when fountain-pens are used, no pressure is necessary. On the contrary, a pressure would create difficulties. The pressure has to be very slight and fluid ink comes out which remains on the paper. This is a significant difference. Therefore, there is a category which exists in writing with a ball-point pen which causes an impression and on the reverse side it's seen as an indentation, whereas the indentation is very slight or there is none if a fountain-pen is used. A fountain-pen would not write properly if too much pressure were exerted. That is a very simple and brief explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. So according -- well, if this document were signed by Naser Oric, he'd have used a fountain-pen; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly signed. You said signed. But, of course, if he has indeed signed, I believe we should speak in those terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Professor. And it may or may not need clarification, but when we speak in English of a fountain-pen you can have a type where you insert a cartridge with a pen -- with ink in it, or there are ones where the pen itself takes up the ink and then writes with it. Which type of pen are we talking about or are they -- or could it be either?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Most probably the fountain-pen which uses a cartridge. However, I did not pursue that examination because it would inquire -- would require invasive examination, whereas the visual examination and the light examination showed that most probably this type of fountain-pen was used. However, if we wanted to establish whether it was the cartridge pen, fountain-pen, or the classical pen, then we would have to apply more invasive examination techniques which we could not do in this case because we would have damaged the integrity of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just to summarise on that, is it correct in fact that by removing [microphone override] document one can analyse the ink, the paper, how far the ink has sunk into the paper and with such invasive techniques find out a great deal more about the document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. There are instruments in place and chemical examinations which can establish this but this would require a more invasive examination approach, as I said. On the basis of the examination carried out, we can establish as follows: That there were two types of pen used, one of which is a fountain-pen, which leaves a trace of ink, whereas the ball-point pen leaves the trace of an ink paste. The ball at the point of the pen rotates and that's how it brings the ink paste on to paper, but there has to be pressure for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now just to come to your conclusions, they are -- firstly you mentioned that this stamp partly covers the signature. You told us yesterday what that indicates to you and so I won't ask you about that again, if your conclusions are again the same, namely, that the stamp should not be over the signature.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The conclusions remain the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, dealing with Hamdija Fejzic and the name Hamdija Fejzic on this document, that's beneath "zapisnicar." Can you just explain to us what that means? Does that mean this person prepared the document or typed the document or what in your language?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the person who keeps minutes from an event. Or that's to say the minutes can be taken down in handwriting and then typed out. In any case, this is an administrative worker who deals with documents. His role was that of an assistant who prepares and processes documents, files documents, keeps the log-books, controls the contents of the documents before they are signed by the person authorised to sign them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. So according to this, Hamdija Fejzic would have prepared this document. Can you tell us about -- again, and it's not necessarily up to me --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I presume my learned friend doesn't want to give evidence in a concluding sense that Hamdija Fejzic would have prepared this document as the witness was just stating what should be considered as the functioning of a secretary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones. Do you want to comment? Do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. Really, it was just anything which is apparent on the face of the document from the word "zapisnicar" and the name, but I don't need to pursue it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Well, it is my objection when Defence counsel gives evidence, made concluding remarks like that, gives leading questions with a view even to certain facts and -- while the witness was just elaborating Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. on the functioning of a secretary, in general what his function is. It's inappropriate questioning in my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, I refer you to line 4 and 5 of page 42, and there is no problems in interpretation here because the words were spoken in English. And Mr. Jones did not say: So according to this, Hamdija Fejzic prepared this document. He said: So according to this, Hamdija Fejzic would have prepared the document. This is -- and in English, that has its connotation. He's not suggesting that indeed because that is what is stated in the paper, therefore it follows that Hamdija Fejzic did prepare. The "would" is there precisely to indicate that that is what appears on the face of the document but doesn't necessarily follow that it is so. In fact, he was -- when you stood up, he said: Can you tell us about it again? And it's not necessarily he was precisely going to indicate --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I accept that, Your Honour, but my advice is that when it comes to facts and conclusions like that, it should not be leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it was a leading question. It's just putting -- anyway, Mr. Jones, I don't know if you want to pursue it any further or not, but I think it's clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I'm really dealing with what on the face of the document that it appears that that person would have been the person who prepared the document, and I'll leave it with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: A question about the grammar in which this document is written. I can draw your attention, for example, to the last three words, "Sarajevu Injima." Is this in good grammatical language? It's the last three words.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This isn't correct. It's grammatically incorrect, completely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, did you analyse or did you compare the signatures on this document with non-contentious signatures of Naser Oric and Hamdija Fejzic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did some of those non-contentious signatures date from 1996, in other words, only three years or so from the contentious ones?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in terms of the non-contentious signatures of Naser Oric and Hamdija Fejzic, were those signatures spontaneous, fast and fluent, or were they otherwise?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What you said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did any of the non-contentious signatures of Naser Oric which you looked at, did any of them have a full stop after the signature?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were so many Naser's signatures covering a very broad span of time, from 1996 up until 2004, and none of the signatures had one, had what we call the punctuation mark when one places a full stop at the end of a word is in this case a punctuation mark, which is in principle placed only at the end of written material. In my practice so far, I've never come across a person's signature at the end of which a punctuation mark is placed. This isn't a sentence. It's a signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. What were your conclusions about whether or not this signature is in fact the signature of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this is an original document, I categorically concluded that it was not written by Naser Oric in his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was that simply because you had the original that you could be categorical or were there any other reasons?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to there having been the original, there were other indicators and elements which arose during the examination, based on the good quality and quantity of non-contentious samples.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, you've told us how the non-contentious signatures which you analysed were spontaneous, fast and fluent. Were the contentious signatures -- I'm not just talking about this document now, I'm leaping ahead slightly. Were the contentious signatures of Naser Oric written spontaneously, quickly and fluently?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were they even written at the same speed, the contentious signatures?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Some of the features of the contentious and non-contentious signatures of Naser Oric set out on pages 30 to 33 of your report?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We don't need to look at that in detail now. I want to ask you about, if you can refer to that later, that's fine. The signature, the alleged signature of Hamdija Fejzic, what did you conclude about that signature?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I concluded that the signature was forged with an unsuccessful method of free-hand imitation and simulation, and I am absolutely sure that this is not Fejzic's signature. This is not Hamdija Fejzic's signature. There are -- such signatures can be found on two more documents that follow after this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We are coming to those. So your conclusions about the alleged signatures of Oric and Fejzic are firm conclusions, they are not probabilistic?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm finished with that document. We can move on to the next document, which is S.2, and it's 02075808, and it's P73. It's questioned signature Q3. And it's dealt with at pages 16 and 17 of Professor Bilic's report. And in order to progress, I'll lead some of this evidence. This was available in the original, for examination. It's typed with some typed corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, yes, your pointing out the alignment "vojna tajna." What can you tell us about that, Professor?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was subsequently typed as was the case with other documents. This is quite recurrent in all the documents. You can see that it is misaligned. It is not aligned with the other pieces of writing. This can be established by mere visualisation. I can show it to you, this way. I do not usually do it this way, but for the sake of clarity, you can see that this part was written earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you've also noted in your report some corrections or changes to this document, in particular at 7 Skelani. Can you tell us how that correction has been made?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can this be focused in please? More, more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it's --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please blow it up a bit more? Yes. At some point, this document contained a completely different typewritten word. What happened next was mechanical scraping or abrasion with an adequate implement. One can see still traces of that earlier word in the form of black dots and abrasions, and even blots of a sort. The word that was there earlier was obliterated and what was subsequently added was the word "Skelana." Whether this was a typographical error which occurred whilst the document was being typed out or whether the reason was different, that is something I cannot conclude anything about. However, what is evident is the scraping effort, the abrasion that can be seen. But it is, of course, up to the Court to enter its findings on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And then moving to your conclusions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You can move ahead with the question. We would like to see this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The conclusion, just to confirm, it's page 36 and it's paragraphs 5 and 7, that the signatures were not signed by Naser Oric and were not signed by Hamdija Fejzic. And, again, are those firm conclusions?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are final, absolute conclusions, under 5 and under 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the next document, I'll just mention it now, to show the witness is S.3, 02075810, and it's also P75. And that's dealt with at pages 16 to 17 of Professor Bilic's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So this document, too, was available for inspection in the original. It's written on one side --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Written, and I'm taking this from your report, commercial writing paper, I believe you say?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And handwritten with -- typed with handwritten corrections in one -- at least one place. Now, can you tell us in this document where there has been a correction to Srebrenica, how has that been made, that correction?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you zoom this in, please? This was covered over with correction fluid and then over the corrected part the word "Srebrenica" was written. However, the punctuation mark of comma was left from the earlier word, and when the word was retyped or typed over, that's when another comma was placed. There is another addition, handwritten addition to the text, quite roughly done. It is quite striking and a bit surprising that such a correction should be done to this type of document, a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And just going back to the mention of correcting fluid, is that what we would call Tipex, that's obviously just one brand. I don't want to promote one brand over another. But what is referred to as Tipex?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correction fluid, white in colour, which is used for errors in a text, and then in order not to scrape the errors, they are covered over in fluid. Had we applied invasive examination techniques, we could have been able to establish perhaps what word was written under. However, we did not apply that type of examination, and we can conclude what we see here, that there was something that was covered over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, as before, and I'm not sure if we dealt with this at S.2 but it's in your report, the signature, the alleged signature by Hamdija Fejzic in ball-point pen and that allegedly by Naser Oric in fountain-pen. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. As was the case with the earlier document, all the observations I relayed in relation to the earlier document apply here.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... your conclusions the same regarding the signatures?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely the same. Fejzic did not sign his name here, as court reporter, nor did Naser Oric sign this particular signature as commander of TO Srebrenica. None of them produced these signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on to S.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are we continuing to 1.45, Your Honour, or do I need to stop again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You stop when you wish, but my idea was to continue until 1.45. However, at this point, I think I would like to know how much time you have left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going it try and finish today. I'm optimistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In that case, do you think you will finish your cross-examination in two days?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If we finish today by my learned friend, then yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Because if not, I have been inquiring to see availability of courtrooms. You know the difficulties that we have at the moment, and I was trying to jump in before others would, and there is a possibility of booking a courtroom for Friday morning, the proviso is that we would have to finish a little bit earlier because one of us needs to travel. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll try and go as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Professor, for the rest of the following documents, I think we can probably --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- take it quite quickly. So we have S.4 where the ERN is 01239504, and it's P4. And this is dealt with at page 17 of your report, available in the original, written only on one side, typed, does this document have any signs of physical or chemical destruction?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the bottom, there is evidence of physical and chemical destruction. This was some substance that permeated the paper and it is now easily torn in that part. So in this part, the document is damaged. On the right-hand margin, as you can see, is torn in parts, whether this was because the document was handled, circulated, used and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And could you in fact confirm your conclusions regarding the signature or the alleged signature of Naser Oric for this document?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we said with regard to the earlier documents applies here, and I stand by my conclusion that this signature was not written by Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this again a question of a signature and a fountain-pen and is it again a question of a signature with a full stop at the end?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was also written in fountain-pen, which has running ink, and we have the punctuation mark, which is a full stop. In this case, as was the case with the other signatures, alleged signatures, the full stop is a bit spaced out. It is further off in relation to the signature, not right at the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it right that in fact there are a whole host of features which you analysed in the signature, not just the full stop that we are referring to?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I listed these features under the comparison that I produced, which is contained on page -- I believe you know which page it is -- that was the C stage, stage of comparison, which is on page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't certain about the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried to present it in a way that would make it easy for everyone to understand. From the perspective of professional ethics, one should not -- an expert should not really state his entire opinion because one can never be sure in whose hands the paper can end up. We can only present those features we are fully certain of. The document examination is time-consuming, it requires a wide range of analyses, looking for both general and specific characteristics, which assist -- or rather, on the basis of which a conclusion is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now we can move to S.5, which is 03720933. It's P176. It's dealt with at pages 17 to 18 of Professor Bilic's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now this was only available for analysis as a photocopy; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This last document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is already in evidence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, this document was available as a photocopy. On pages 17 to 18 of your report, you express reservations about working with photocopies and you don't need to elaborate on that now. But is it right that you have those reservations about giving an opinion in relation to copies?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We can -- if need be, we can elaborate on that subsequently. But for now, I just want to ask you the following about this document. Firstly, the "vonja tajna strogo pov," is it the same as before, that that does not align with the other words in the document or does it line up?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was typed in later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I do have reservation. It's a photocopy. When one photocopies, there can always be extensions. It can be misleading. It all depends on how you place the document, what the quality of the photocopying paper is, what the toner was like, and so on and so forth, whether the document is being photocopied with a view to achieving something, and modern photocopying machines are such that everything can be made to look as if it were authentic. And that's my general remark about photocopying. So to carry out any subtle measurements or analyses on photocopies is highly uncertain. That's why I don't wish to decidedly state my opinion about this. And the fact that I have analysed this signature is a precedent in my case. That's why I say most probably. Because if you only look at the shape, the form of the signature, and if we go back to all the signatures we have, I think even a layperson can see that it's different, and there is nothing one can add or take away. That's why I used the category most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just for clarity, the conclusion most probably not the signature of Naser Oric, and you used that measure of probability because you had only a copy?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you we can move to the next document, which is S.6, and that's 01839608, and it's P37. It's also been designated Q17. And it's dealt with at pages 18 to 19 of Professor Bilic's report. This was available in the original, written only on one side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And can you tell us if there is a water-mark?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a water-mark on this document. There is a water-mark. The one we've come across before. Extra Post with a chamois on a rock, and we have explained the origin of this type of paper, and what the water-mark means. You can see this for yourself. Extra Post, Extra Post, Extra Post. You can see it easily. This is half of an A4 size paper. It has been torn in half. And this is high quality writing paper. You can take a look, if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your conclusion was that this was not the signature of Naser Oric and that was a firm conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is a final conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I propose to move on to the next document but, of course, if Your Honours wish to see the water-mark, the chamois on a rock, otherwise I know Your Honours will have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can proceed. We will have these documents available later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. It's more important to finish with the testimony of this expert today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So we are now moving to S.7, and this is 01239545, P158, it's Q24, and it's dealt with at page 19 of your report, available in the original, as we can see. Here the stamp does not cover the signature. Conversely is says Nasre Oric. Now, what was your conclusion about this signature?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion regarding this signature is also that it was not written in hand by Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we come to S.8, and that's 03721400, and it's P210. It's designated Q30. Dealt with at pages 17 to 18 of your report but again only available as a photocopy. Did you conclude this was most probably not the signature of Naser Oric and you used that level of probability because it's a photocopy?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move on to S.9, which is 03721419, and it's P213. It's dealt with at pages 17 to 18 of your report. And again, we can take this quickly, I think, because it's a photocopy, and you reached the conclusion most probably not the signature of Naser Oric. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes. Most probably not signed by Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You also noted a change or correction "Zulfaroli" in your report. Can you notice how that change was made to that word?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you zoom in a little, please? You can see this quite clearly, although it's a photocopy, so one can rarely see something like this, photocopies are only black and white. But here you can see that "Zulfaroli," I don't see the sense of this. There is an error as we can see, and it's added in later, "Zulfaroli."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. In terms of the space between the signature line and the rest of the document, is that within the parameters of what in your experience is normal or reasonable or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an enormous space left here. Whether it was left so that something could be written in subsequently, it's an unnecessarily large space for this text. Two or three spaces might have been left. This is characteristic of all these documents, and indirectly, speaks about those who created these documents. They always left a space. Whether it was in handwriting or in typewriting, they left a large space, which gives rise to suspicion.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We will move on to the next document, which is S.10, and that's 01239528. It's P13. It's also Q15. It's dealt with at pages 18 to 19 of your report. As we can see, it was available in the original. And can you tell us about any water-mark, first of all?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document. I want to look at the water-mark once again. You can't see it unless you hold it up to the light. Yes. There is a water-mark here with a text "Extra Post," and it shows a chamois on a rock, just as in the previous document which was on half a sheet of A4-size paper. So this appears to be half of that sheet of paper. Is there anything else we need to say about these documents? Do you have any further questions about them?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I believe you also note in your report that there is an imprint on this document with the name Oric. I don't know if you're able to show that on the ELMO. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you zoom in, please? Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Apparently it's not possible to zoom.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoom in, please. Yes, yes, zoom in, zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We can stop. We can just about see it.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, okay, okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, can you just explain what you see there for us?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in block writing, in Cyrillic letters, O-R-I-C. It's block writing, not block capitals but block writing. You can see it even better. If Their Honours wish to see it, please take it to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you bring it here, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Show it to Mr. Wubben, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. Also I don't think we need to necessarily go into it now but on page 32 of your report, for S.9 I think you point out some of the features -- sorry, S.10, some of the features which you -- the contentious signature which led you to your conclusions about the signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I marked these characteristics, only those that can indicate to anyone, Their Honours, counsel, whoever wishes to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. That's fine. We will look at that at our leisure. Just want to ask you to confirm your conclusion about the signature on this document as stated in your report, namely not the signature of Naser Oric and that being a firm conclusion, not a probabilistic one.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. We can move to S.11. S.11, which is 00926461. It's P3, and it's also Q10, and it's dealt with at pages 17 to 18 of Professor Bilic's report. And again, I think I can summarise most of what's in your report, available only as a photocopy, and therefore you concluded that it was probably not the signature of Naser Oric. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And is there anything you can tell us about the letters POV, P-O-V full stop, which appears also on this document in the first line?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time this abbreviation is used in one of the documents. It's written incorrectly with a small P and a capital OV. From what I know about such texts, it's the first part of the word "povjerjevo," [phoen] meaning confidential. But it doesn't make much sense in this position. This is a photocopy. We see quite a few alterations, as we can in all the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. We can move to S.12. The ERN is 01239544. And it's P14. It's also Q18. And it's dealt with at pages 18 to 19 of your report, available in the original. And, first of all, I think we can deal immediately with your conclusion that this was not the signature of Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you to pay attention to the words written in the top right-hand corner to the president of the War Presidency. Now, does that align with the rest of the text? Is there anything else you can tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is added on later. Take a look. This has been typed in subsequently, after the entire document was written, as you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So, in other words, yes, the words, "the president of the War Presidency," you're saying were added later because it doesn't align with what's typed on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, I'm finished with that document. We can move to S.13. That's 01801596. It's P330. And it's dealt with at pages 17 to 18 of your report. And again, available only as a photocopy, and so your conclusion was most probably not the signature of Naser Oric; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And that two other features which I'll ask you about, again the space before the signature line. Does that seem normal or abnormal to you?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Abnormal. This space here is very big between the text and the signature. As the document is photocopied, there is nothing further we can conclude about it. But you can see how large this space is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: On the left-hand side we see the words "prekucani tekst." What in fact does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The text was typed and then it was retyped again. It was retyped from a pre-existing text, which may have been either handwritten or typewritten or printed out or -- it may have been a facsimile, but we do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm finished with those documents. I have a few general subjects which I think we can cover today. There will be a couple more exhibits to look at. But firstly -- Professor, in the contentious signatures of Naser Oric, did you find variation in the signature or not?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of the contentious signatures, there was a variation from signature to signature, every time. This variation was unexpected when dealing with a signature of a single person and a single personality. These are signatures that differ from each other completely. You can see this on the map I have created if you look carefully at the contested signatures, and you can observe this without much difficulty.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. There are a few last documents which I would like to show. Can you just give us the page numbers, Professor, for reference?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the map? 30, 31, 32 and 33. All these pages make up a single system and they are provided as a whole in continuity.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there are a few other documents I want to show you and to hopefully forestall any objections from the Prosecution, because Mr. Wubben did mention a possible objection earlier, it's purely to show the existence of water-marks on some other documents, and these documents not analysed in the report, and it's merely a question of noting a water-mark. And I can read out by ERN number -- I understand the documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what's the purpose of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's to have the witness confirm that there are the water-marks and whether they -- how they compare to the other water-marks he's seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The first document is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, I have an objection, Your Honour. We are not prepared for this when it comes to comparison now here, what kind of expertise for comparison in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will assess the importance of this later because for the time being I am not, at least speaking for myself, in a position to make a definitive assessment. What's your position? We will proceed for the time being, and then if we feel that this is an unnecessary exercise or one which deserves to be -- deserves the objection of Mr. Wubben, then obviously we will stop you. But let's proceed for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's four documents, I think. The first is 02075716. And this is the original of P53, so that will be in the -- in those files, which the Registry has. And the others -- my apologies if this is going to be difficult to find them, but I'll read the other numbers in the meantime. Then there is 02075745, 02075762, and 02075765. And I did earlier check that they are -- they will be in that collection of documents. In fact, while the Registry is locating those documents, I do have another question for Professor Bilic, a general question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Professor Bilic, in terms of the documents that you've analysed in your report, you referred to a number of features which recur in all of the documents, or in many of them, the covering of the signature by the stamp, alterations and mistakes, typing errors, different versions of the contentious Hamed Salihovic signature, variation in the Naser Oric contentious signature, misalignment of words in the header. Taken as a whole, is this in your opinion indicative of anything? Are you able to give a globalistic conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Examining the entire sample of all the contentious documents, what you have said was established, both in general, in my view, these are all suspect documents that have not been signed by their real authors, those who should have signed them, in which unknown writers have participated, and I reiterate that these are suspicious, suspicious, suspicious documents. And Their Honours will evaluate this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. I think if we are ready with any of those documents which I mentioned we can take them one at a time. Perhaps I'll ask if you put it on the ELMO and then we can read the ERN number one by one rather than me calling out the ERN number. Right. So we have 02075716. Can you just tell us, Professor, please, if there is a water-mark and if so, what type?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this paper, there is a water-mark. It's a sail-boat again. It's down the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this is a document of the Srebrenica war hospital purportedly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says here. You can see it clearly, Srebrenica war hospital, date 19th of March, 1993, record of an on-site inspection concerning the death of Sekulic, son of Milorad, Branko.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That is purportedly signed by Dr. Avdo Hasanovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness is asked to confirm something factual, nothing to do with his alleged expertise, like and purportedly Dr. Avdo Hasanovic signed this, to confirm that. It has no indication, relevancy, it's really not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you. That's not important.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Purportedly is simply on the face of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not important.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We'd say Your Honours follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, the whole thing is that point made is basically we have another document with the sailing-boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Purportedly from the war hospital signed by Dr. Hasanovic, that's my point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, every time my learned friend now goes beyond the water-mark issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, I think you are missing it completely. We are talking of documents that were supposedly prepared more or less at the same time, and also more or less in the same place. So let's move. You know what we are saying. Let's proceed. We have only got six minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, and just three more documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So the next one is 02075765. Again, if you could, please, quickly, if you're able to, Professor, confirm any water-mark?

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document also says it comes from the Srebrenica war hospital, and it's a record of an on-site inspection regarding the death of a person, and we will look at it now. Yes, there is a water-mark here, a sail-boat, on this document. You can look at it, if you like. It might be a good idea if you were to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next document. We'll have a look at all these documents. Are these in evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the originals are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, the originals wouldn't be probably, but Mr. Wubben can enlighten us on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Some of them are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben, are these --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this document is in evidence, in my opinion, P68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And the previous one should -- P53, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, they are all exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I thank you so much, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we are interested in the water-mark. Please tell us whether it has a water-mark, and the reference is 02075745. And we'll see for ourselves what the document states on the face of it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has a water-mark with a sail-boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then finally 02075762.

utterances.speaker: ESAD BILIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same as before. There is a water-mark with a sail-boat.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much. I think we can give you a break now, Professor Bilic. You can go back to your hotel. You're not to communicate with anyone on the substance of your testimony.
